First, we constrain the attention so that occluded ("void") tokens attend only to known-healthy tokens of the same volume, with a learned bias toward each query's contralateral homologue, forcing the completion to be inferred from observed anatomy rather than from other unknown regions. Second, we add a contralateral-symmetry input that supplies the mirrored healthy hemisphere as a patient-specific prior; since the brain is approximately bilaterally symmetric and lesions are typically unilateral, this prior improves the distortion metrics at matched structural similarity. On the official BraTS-2026 validation leaderboard our submission reaches a mean healthy-region SSIM of $0.864$, PSNR of $24.7$\,dB and MSE of $4.6{\times}10^{-3}$ over $219$ cases. We further analyse the residual smoothness inherent to distortion-optimal regression and discuss its implications for anatomical realism.

</details>


### [52] [ViP-Rig: Visual-Prompted Controllable Rigging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27982)
*Zihan Qin,Mingze Sun,Yifan Mao,Jialei Xu,Jingfeng Guo,Changrong Hu,Wenbo Zhao,Junjun Jiang,Xianming Liu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ViP-Rig introduces a visual-prompted rigging framework that conditions a frozen backbone with dense-to-compact visual prompts to perform skeleton generation and skinning prediction, enabling prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing with explicit control and improved accuracy over geometry-only baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Rigging is inherently task-dependent and current automatic rigs offer limited explicit control over skeletons and deformation behavior, necessitating an interactive mechanism to inject user intent into pretrained models.

Method: Two-stage pipeline: Skeleton Generation uses Dense-to-Compact Visual Prompt Encoding to produce fixed-length tokens injected into a frozen autoregressive generator via gated adapters to determine joint placement and branching; Skinning Prediction uses the same encoding for rigidity prompts, injecting tokens into point and joint streams to modulate point–joint compatibility and skinning weights, with backbones kept frozen.

Result: On Articulation-XL2.0 and zero-shot ModelsResource evaluation, ViP-Rig more accurately recovers target skeletons and skinning weights than geometry-conditioned baselines; qualitative results show explicit, localized control in both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing.

Conclusion: Visual prompting with frozen backbones enables explicit, localized control in rigging, achieving improved alignment with target rigs and skinning while preserving geometric priors and supporting user-guided editing.

Abstract: Rigging is inherently task-dependent because the same mesh may require different skeletons and deformation behaviors across animation tasks. In practice, artists often inspect an initial rig and repeatedly edit its skeletal structure and deformation behavior to meet specific animation requirements. Existing automatic methods primarily generate a plausible rig from geometry, offering limited explicit control over the resulting skeleton and deformation behavior. In this work, we present ViP-Rig, a visual-prompted framework that supports both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing by injecting features extracted from user-drawn or edited 2D skeletal and rigidity prompts into frozen pretrained backbones. Specifically, ViP-Rig consists of two stages, Skeleton Generation and Skinning Prediction. In the first stage, the skeletal sketch is processed by the Dense-to-Compact Visual Prompt Encoding to produce compact, fixed-length conditioning tokens. The resulting tokens are injected into a frozen pretrained autoregressive generator through gated adapters to control joint placement and branching structure while preserving the generator's geometric prior. In the second stage, the rigidity map is processed using the same visual encoding design, while the pretrained skinning backbone remains frozen. The resulting tokens are symmetrically injected into the point and joint streams to modulate point-joint compatibility and the resulting skinning weights. Experiments on Articulation-XL2.0 and zero-shot evaluation on ModelsResource show that ViP-Rig more accurately recovers target skeletons and skinning weights than geometry-conditioned baselines under prompt-guided evaluation. Qualitative results further demonstrate explicit and localized control in both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing.

</details>


### [53] [Deep learning-based hierarchical insect classification using camera trap imagery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28005)
*Zaki Mahfoud,Juan A. Chiavassa,Simon Walther,Florian Haselbeck,Ehsan Yaghoubi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A deep learning hierarchical classifier trained on a curated, long-tailed insect image dataset improves taxonomy-level predictions by leveraging a five-level taxonomy, using class-balanced weighting and a confidence-based depth choice, achieving 80–99% per-level accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Insect biodiversity monitoring is challenged by declines, lack of standardized data, and costly manual identifications; scalable, non-lethal camera-trap data require automated, generalizable classifiers that handle imbalanced data and hierarchical taxonomy.

Method: Construct a manually curated ~1M image dataset from 1,801 camera-trap videos annotated with a five-level, 34-class hierarchy; adapt a hierarchical classification model to a variable-depth five-level hierarchy with class-balanced weighting; enforce hierarchy-consistent predictions and use a confidence threshold (T=0.6) to determine depth of prediction.

Result: Outperforms non-hierarchical classifiers by exploiting taxonomy to extract granularity-specific features; produces hierarchy-consistent predictions at the deepest level meeting the threshold; per-level accuracy 80–99% across five levels.

Conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of scalable, taxonomy-aware deep learning for insect biodiversity monitoring and highlights the value of hierarchical, confidence-aware prediction strategies on long-tailed datasets; shows promise for scaling monitoring with automated camera-trap data, though generalization to other taxa and field conditions remains to be explored.

Abstract: Declining insect populations make reliable biodiversity monitoring increasingly urgent, yet monitoring of insect biodiversity is hampered by a lack of standardised data and by costly and time-consuming manual identification by expert entomologists. Deep learning-based image classifiers, processing data from automated non-lethal camera traps, have the potential to transform and scale insect biodiversity monitoring. However, challenges remain in acquiring expert-annotated datasets, developing model architectures that generalise well across diverse taxonomic levels and training models on highly imbalanced data. Hierarchical data also benefits from designing models that default to higher-confidence, coarser-level predictions, when uncertain about finer taxonomic levels. In this paper we address these challenges with a deep learning-based hierarchical classification model. First, we present a manually curated, long-tailed dataset of around one million images of insects, extracted from 1,801 camera-trap video recordings and annotated with a five-level, 34-class hierarchy. Further, we adapt a hierarchical classification model architecture to a five-level variable-depth hierarchy, with class-balanced weighting. Our model improves on non-hierarchical classifiers by leveraging biological taxonomy to extract granularity-specific visual features and makes hierarchy-consistent predictions to the deepest taxonomic level that meets a confidence threshold (T = 0.6). Our model achieved a per-level accuracy of 80-99% on test data, across five levels of hierarchy. Furthermore ...

</details>


### [54] [Beyond Classification: Pathology Foundation Models as Detection Encoders for Mitotic Figures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28007)
*Sweta Banerjee,Alireza Teimoury,Nils Porsche,Alexandra K. Stoll,Viktoria Weiss,Niklas Hargarter,Jonas Ammeling,Thomas Conrad,Christoph Stroblberger,Christopher Kaltnecker,Robert Klopfleisch,Christof A. Bertram,Katharina Breininger,Marc Aubreville*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Pathology foundation models (FMs) can serve as effective backbones for dense mitotic-figure detection when combined with RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, or Deformable DETR; H-optimus-0 and Virchow are particularly competitive and may offer out-of-domain robustness; code is publicly available.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To determine whether latent spaces of current self-supervised pathology foundation models provide discriminant, spatially resolved features suitable for dense object detection, not just classification.

Method: Evaluate six FMs (UNI, UNI2-h, Virchow, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, H-optimus-1) as backbones for three detector architectures (RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, Deformable DETR) on the MIDOG++ multi-domain dataset and the TUPAC16 dataset (out-of-domain), compared against an end-to-end ResNet50 baseline.

Result: H-optimus-0 and Virchow achieve competitive performance, indicating FM latent spaces trained with image-level self-supervision are suitable for direct mitotic figure detection and may exhibit slight robustness to out-of-domain data.

Conclusion: Pathology foundation-model backbones can effectively support dense mitosis detection, with potential generalization benefits; reinforces value of self-supervised latent representations for downstream detection tasks; code released at the cited GitHub repository.

Abstract: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are models trained on vast amounts of typically unlabeled data and have been shown to yield regularized latent spaces that can be used effectively in downstream classification tasks. This is also true for the classification of mitotic figures vs. other cells. However, it is so far unclear if the latent space of current FMs provides features that are discriminant and spatially suitably resolved to also serve as a backbone for dense object detection paradigms. In this work, we investigate this question for common current pathology FMs (UNI, UNI2-h, Virchow, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, H-optimus-1) and compare their performance against a fully end-to-end trained baseline based on a ResNet50 architecture. We combine FM backbones with representatives of single stage, dual stage and self-attention-based detectors (RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, Deformable DETR respectively) on the multi-domain MIDOG++ dataset, and on the TUPAC16 dataset as an out-of-domain case. We show that the H-optimus-0 and Virchow models yielded competitive performance, indicating that the latent spaces of current FMs, all trained on image-level self-supervision, are suitable for direct mitotic figure detection and may be slightly more robust on our out-of-domain test case. All code is made available publicly at https://github.com/DeepMicroscopy/FM4MFdet.

</details>


### [55] [ENCORE: Event-Assisted Complementary Motion Refinement for Learned Video Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28020)
*Shuhan Ye,Hongbin Yu,Chenqi Kong,Pingchuan Ma,Chong Wang,Jun Wan,Qixin Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ENCORE leverages asynchronous event data to refine RGB-based motion estimation in learned video compression, using Complementary Motion Representation (CMR), Spatial Energy and Redundancy-Informed Calibration (SERIC), and Energy-Aware Routing (EAR) to improve rate–distortion performance without changing the RGB coding target.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Conventional learned codecs infer motion solely from RGB frames, making them sensitive to fast motion, blur, occlusion, weak textures, low illumination, and abrupt brightness changes. Event cameras offer fine-grained intensity changes aligned to RGB timestamps, providing complementary motion evidence to enhance temporal modeling.

Method: 1) Complementary Motion Representation (CMR): decompose aligned RGB–event features into common and modality-specific motion representations. 2) SERIC: identify event-specific, active and novel responses relative to RGB, suppress weak/redundant evidence, and predict a candidate flow correction. 3) Energy-Aware Routing (EAR): determine where and how strongly the correction should refine the RGB flow. RGB remains the sole coding target; events act as an auxiliary motion signal. Evaluated on BS-ERGB, HQ-EVFI, and CED datasets, with varying GOP lengths.

Result: ENCORE yields consistent gains across datasets: on BS-ERGB it achieves up to 20.80% PSNR-RGB and 22.14% MS-SSIM-RGB BD-rate savings, with clear improvements on the other two datasets as well.

Conclusion: Integrating event data for motion refinement substantially improves learned video compression by refining RGB flow without altering the RGB coding target, demonstrating effective multi-modal fusion for temporal modeling in compression.

Abstract: Learned video compression relies on accurate temporal modeling to remove redundancy between adjacent frames. However, most existing codecs infer motion solely from discretely sampled RGB frames, making their estimates vulnerable to fast motion, blur, occlusion, weak texture, low illumination, and abrupt brightness changes. Event cameras asynchronously capture fine-grained intensity changes between RGB timestamps and therefore provide complementary evidence about inter-frame dynamics. We propose ENCORE, an Event-Assisted Complementary Motion Refinement framework for learned video compression. ENCORE first employs Complementary Motion Representation (CMR) to decompose aligned RGB-event features into common and modality-specific motion representations. Spatial Energy and Redundancy-Informed Calibration (SERIC) then identifies event-specific responses that are active and novel relative to RGB, suppresses weak or redundant evidence, and predicts a candidate flow correction. Finally, Energy-Aware Routing (EAR) determines where and how strongly the correction should refine the RGB flow. Events serve solely as an auxiliary modality for motion modeling, while RGB remains the only coding and reconstruction target. Experiments on BS-ERGB, HQ-EVFI, and CED demonstrate consistent gains across datasets and GOP lengths. On BS-ERGB, ENCORE achieves up to 20.80% PSNR-RGB and 22.14% MS-SSIM-RGB BD-rate savings, while retaining clear improvements on the other two datasets.

</details>


### [56] [Split and Drive: Dual-Axis Disentanglement for Real-Time Gaussian Head Avatars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28032)
*MD Wahiduzzaman Khan,Mingshan Jia,Xiaolin Zhang,En Yu,Kaska Musial-Gabrys*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SpiD (Split and Drive) introduces a two-axis disentangled single-image Gaussian head avatar framework. It uses a compute axis to internalize per-frame driving (no external tracker) and a feature axis that splits the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches for geometrically distinct facial domains. It achieves strong state-of-the-art results and fastest single-GPU inference when the full driving pipeline is included.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome latency and expressiveness limitations of existing 3D Gaussian Splatting methods that rely on external tracking and entangle facial regions; enable real-time, high-fidelity head avatars from a single image without external dependencies.

Method: Two disentanglement axes: (1) compute axis to internalize per-frame driving and remove external tracking at inference; (2) feature axis decomposes the avatar into three Gaussian branches, each modeling a geometrically distinct facial domain; integrates into a Gaussian head avatar pipeline with a complete driving pipeline included.

Result: Extensive experiments show SpiD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and delivers the fastest inference speed among the compared methods on a single GPU when the full driving pipeline is included.

Conclusion: SpiD provides a compact, expressive, and fast single-image Gaussian head avatar by decoupling driving from geometry across three facial domains, removing external tracking requirements and achieving state-of-the-art performance with fastest end-to-end inference.

Abstract: Creating photorealistic animatable head avatars from a single image remains a fundamental challenge in digital human synthesis. While recent 3D Gaussian Splatting methods have achieved promising results, they rely on external tracking pipelines whose latency is excluded from inference measurements. Furthermore, they adopt unified representations that entangle geometrically distinct facial regions, limiting both expressiveness and rendering fidelity. We propose SpiD (Split and Drive), a single-image Gaussian head avatar framework built on two disentanglement axes. The compute axis internalizes per-frame driving, eliminating external tracking dependency at inference. The feature axis decomposes the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches, each modeling a geometrically distinct facial domain. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistently strong performance against state-of-the-art methods while achieving the fastest inference speed among all compared methods on a single GPU with the complete driving pipeline included.

</details>


### [57] [TongueReenact: Geometry-Anchored Tongue Synthesis for Face Reenactment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28039)
*MD Wahiduzzaman Khan,Mingshan Jia,Xiaolin Zhang,En Yu,Kaska Musial-Gabrys*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer for face reenactment. Introduces a foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping pipeline to produce a tongue segmentation model without curated annotations, and a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for realistic tongue synthesis with adaptive mask dilation for seamless mouth boundaries. Demonstrates >2x improvements on tongue-specific metrics and validates perceptual superiority with a VLM-based evaluation protocol across ablations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the neglected tongue dynamics in speech and expressive facial reenactment, which leads to anatomically inconsistent mouth interiors and reduced realism.

Method: 1) Foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping to create a dedicated tongue segmentation model without curated annotations. 2) Spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for tongue synthesis with adaptive mask dilation to ensure smooth transitions at mouth boundaries.

Result: Empirical results show more than twofold improvements over baselines on all tongue-specific metrics. A VLM-based evaluation protocol corroborates perceptual superiority across ablations.

Conclusion: Tongue dynamics can be effectively transferred in cross-identity face reenactment using the proposed annotation-free segmentation and diffusion-based synthesis pipeline, achieving substantial gains in both objective tongue metrics and perceptual quality.

Abstract: Modern face reenactment systems achieve impressive pose and expression transfer using geometry-driven representations. However, they largely ignore tongue dynamics, leading to anatomically inconsistent mouth interiors during speech and expressive motions. We introduce the first framework for cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer in face reenactment. We propose a foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping pipeline that produces a dedicated tongue segmentation model for in-the-wild reenactment without curated annotations. We further introduce a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for realistic tongue synthesis, with adaptive mask dilation for seamless mouth boundary transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate improvements of more than two times over all baselines on every tongue-specific metric. We additionally propose a VLM-based evaluation protocol that replicates expert annotation at scale, confirming perceptual superiority across all ablation variants.

</details>


### [58] [Temporal Concentration from Rollout Errors: Implicit Preference Optimization for Text-to-Video Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28058)
*Henglin Liu,Fangyuan Kong,Jing Wang,Yizhou Lin,Nisha Huang,Chang Liu,Xintao Wang,Pengfei Wan,Kun Gai,Xiu Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: cIPO introduces implicit preference signals derived from the denoising process and concentrates post-training optimization on high-error, temporally sparse segments to reduce artifacts in diffusion-based video generation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Temporal artifacts (motion collapse, flickering, oversaturation) persist due to two bottlenecks: (i) preference attribution—offline annotations are costly and misrepresent learning dynamics; online rewards are rollout-aware but unstable and biased; (ii) temporal credit misallocation—uniform supervision fails to target brief failure segments.

Method: During post-training, add forward noise to real videos and reconstruct via iterative denoising. Treat the original video as the preferred sample and its reconstruction as the dispreferred one. Use frame-level discrepancies to compute temporal reconstruction errors and concentrate optimization on high-error segments to fix failure-prone regions.

Result: Extensive experiments report improvements in video authenticity and temporal coherence across multiple datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of implicit preference with temporally concentrated optimization.

Conclusion: Implicit preference signals derived from denoising, combined with temporally concentrated optimization, effectively enhance video diffusion models without requiring additional human annotations or external reward models.

Abstract: Recent advances in preference alignment for diffusion-based video generation, particularly via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), have significantly improved visual quality. However, temporally sparse artifacts such as motion collapse, object flickering, and color oversaturation remain a major barrier to perceptual realism. Existing methods struggle with these issues due to two key limitations: (1) the preference attribution bottleneck, where offline human annotations are costly and fail to accurately capture learning dynamics, while online reward signals are rollout-aware but often unstable and biased; and (2) temporal credit misallocation, where uniformly applied supervision cannot effectively target the brief segments in which artifacts occur. To address these challenges, we propose concentrated Implicit Preference Optimization (cIPO), a post-training framework for video diffusion models. cIPO derives implicit preference signals directly from the denoising process: given a real video, the model adds forward noise and reconstructs it via iterative denoising, treating the original as the preferred sample and the reconstruction as the dispreferred one. This formulation captures inference-time errors without requiring human annotations or external reward models. Moreover, frame-level discrepancies between original and reconstructed videos reveal when failures occur. cIPO leverages this by computing temporal reconstruction errors and concentrating optimization on high-error segments, enabling more precise correction of failure-prone regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that cIPO consistently enhances video authenticity and temporal coherence across multiple datasets, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of implicit preference with temporally concentrated optimization.

</details>


### [59] [Landmark shape spaces with induced metrics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28064)
*Sarang Joshi,Peter W. Michor,Stefan Sommer*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A unified landmark shape space framework that merges Kendall's landmark shape spaces with right-invariant Sobolev metrics on the diffeomorphism group via a screened elasticity operator; yields collision-avoiding, scale-fixed, and rigid-motion-invariant geometry for arbitrary landmark counts with computable geodesics.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To combine the invariances of Kendall's landmark shape spaces with the smooth, collision-avoiding metrics induced by right-invariant Sobolev metrics on the diffeomorphism group, enabling robust, scale-fixed landmark-based shape analysis that is independent of the number of landmarks.

Method: Introduce the screened elasticity operator whose null-space is exactly the rigid motions, descend the right-invariant Sobolev metric from the diffeomorphism group to the space of landmark configurations, derive the induced geometry on landmark spaces, and develop approaches for matching and numerical computation of geodesics.

Result: The resulting landmark shape spaces inherit: (i) metric regularity preventing landmark collisions, (ii) ambient-space metric defined independently of the number of landmarks, (iii) preservation of local rigid transformations, (iv) removal of global rigid motions, and (v) fixed scale; enabling practical matching and geodesic computation while retaining Kendall-style invariances.

Conclusion: The framework provides a robust, scalable, and invariant geometric structure for landmark-based shape analysis, unifying Kendall's shape-space invariances with Sobolev-regular, ambient-metric landmark spaces, with applicable numerical methods for matching and geodesics.

Abstract: We present a unification of Kendall's landmark shape spaces, where rigid motions are factored out and scale fixed on landmark configurations equipped with Euclidean geometry, with landmark configuration spaces carrying Riemannian metrics descending from right-invariant Sobolev metrics on the diffeomorphism group. The resulting new landmark shape spaces achieve the defining properties of both approaches: The regularity of the descending metric prevents landmarks from colliding, the metric is defined in the ambient space independent of the number of landmarks, local rigid transformations are preserved, global rigid motions are removed, and scale fixed. To achieve this, we define a particular Sobolev-type operator, the screened elasticity operator, whose null-space consists exactly of the rigid motions, we show how this operator descends to achieve the desired geometry, and we present approaches to solving matching problems and computing geodesics numerically. The resulting construction allows the use of landmark configuration spaces with sufficiently regular metrics in applications while retaining the shape invariances that are a hallmark of Kendall's shape spaces.

</details>


### [60] [BladeYOLO: Wind Turbine Blade Defect Detection with Limited Annotations and Weak-Saliency Awareness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28065)
*Yabin Xu,Fangtao Zhang,Fan Wang,Zhan Wang,Honghua Chen,Mingqiang Wei,Haoran Xie,Sam Kwong*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: BladeYOLO is a ViT-equipped, transformer-based YOLO variant for wind turbine blade defect detection, adding Mamba-guided enhancement and a Fourier-based Style-Injector to improve accuracy and robustness under limited data and varying environments; achieves cross-dataset gains.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Detection of blade defects is hindered by limited on-site data, small and low-contrast defects, and complex backgrounds; robust transfer of generic visual priors is needed to improve detection under limited annotations.

Method: Replace the YOLOv12-L backbone with a ViT pretrained by DINOv3; introduce Mamba-guided Weak-Defect Enhancement with a Detail-Enhanced Multi-scale Branch and Cross-Mamba to propagate high-level semantics to shallow features; add a lightweight Style-Injector using Fourier decomposition to inject environment style into ViT self-attention; train and evaluate on WTBlade-Defect with annotation-budget experiments; further validate cross-dataset robustness on Wind Surface Defect dataset.

Result: BladeYOLO achieves superior performance on the WTBlade-Defect dataset; annotation-budget experiments show robust performance under reduced annotations; on the public Wind Surface Defect dataset, BladeYOLO outperforms the best competing method by 3.5% in mAP50 and 2.5% in mAP50-95, indicating strong cross-dataset robustness.

Conclusion: The integration of a DINOv3-initialized ViT backbone with specialized Mamba enhancement and a Fourier-based style injector yields a robust blade defect detector that performs well under limited data and across datasets, offering a viable solution for practical wind-turbine blade inspection.

Abstract: Wind turbine blade defect detection remains highly challenging in real-world inspection scenarios due to limited on-site data and the subtle visual characteristics of defects. In practice, blade defects are often small-scale, low-contrast, and difficult to distinguish from complex backgrounds, which significantly limits the robustness of existing detectors. To address these challenges, we propose BladeYOLO, a defect detection framework for wind turbine blades. Specifically, we integrate a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone initialized with DINOv3 self-supervised pre-trained weights into YOLOv12-L, enabling the transfer of large-scale generic visual priors to blade defect detection and improving feature representation under limited training annotations. To enhance the perception of subtle defects, we further develop a Mamba-guided Weak-Defect Enhancement module, which consists of a Detail-Enhanced Multi-scale Branch for preserving high-frequency structural cues and a Cross-Mamba module for progressively propagating high-level semantic guidance to shallow features. In addition, we introduce a lightweight Style-Injector module that captures environment-related style information via Fourier decomposition and injects it into selected ViT self-attention layers, thereby improving robustness against environment-induced appearance variations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BladeYOLO achieves superior performance on the WTBlade-Defect dataset, with additional annotation-budget experiments showing its favorable performance under reduced training annotations. Evaluation on the public Wind Surface Defect dataset further provides supportive evidence for the cross-dataset robustness of BladeYOLO. In particular, on this public dataset, BladeYOLO outperforms the best competing method by 3.5\% in mAP$_{50}$ and 2.5\% in mAP$_{50-95}$.

</details>


### [61] [mmRadarTwin: A Measurement-Calibrated Signal-Level Digital Twin Platform for Indoor mmWave Radar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28108)
*Jianyi Zhou,Chenghao Zhang,Yanli Li,Dong Yuan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: mmRadarTwin is a signal-level digital twin for indoor mmWave radar that links real measurements with Unreal Engine scene simulations to produce per-path, path-attributed results for accurate comparison with FMCW data; evaluated with 154 poses across 22 radar locations, achieving 70.8% recall of geometry-supported response regions and enabling diagnosis of residual discrepancies.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Indoor mmWave radar perception is hard to reproduce due to dependence on scene geometry, materials, multipath, hardware conventions, and signal processing; existing ray-tracing/digital twins expose only high-level quantities not aligned with radar signal products, hindering faithful validation and debugging.

Method: A combined real-measurement branch and Unreal Engine scene-simulation branch connected via a shared receive-channel and range-angle processing interface. The simulator outputs complex multi-channel receive grids and per-path contribution records (actor, material tag, propagation event, output-bin) for each simulated return.

Result: In an office deployment, 154 measured poses over 22 radar locations yielded a recall of 70.8% of geometry-supported response regions in the central usable field of view when using a physics-only path-basis simulator. Residuals arose from weak/missing path support, shifted responses, unsupported anchors, and missing physical mechanisms.

Conclusion: mmRadarTwin provides a practical workflow for constructing, comparing, and diagnosing indoor radar digital twins, rather than claiming full map reconstruction or cross-room generalization.

Abstract: Indoor mmWave radar perception is difficult to reproduce because measured range-angle responses depend on scene geometry, material response, multipath, hardware conventions, and signal processing. Existing ray-tracing and digital-twin tools often expose rendering, channel, or path-level quantities, while radar sensing requires complex signal products that can be processed and compared in the same domain as real FMCW measurements. We present mmRadarTwin, a signal-level and path-attributed digital-twin platform for indoor mmWave radar. mmRadarTwin links a real radar measurement branch with an Unreal Engine scene-simulation branch through a shared receive-channel and range-angle processing interface. The simulator writes complex multi-channel receive grids and exports per-path contribution records that identify the actor, material tag, propagation event, and output-bin support of each simulated return. We evaluate mmRadarTwin in an office deployment using a commodity monostatic mmWave radar and mobile scene-capture hardware. Across 154 measured poses spanning 22 radar locations, the current physics-only path-basis simulator recalls 70.8% of measurement-active geometry-supported response regions in the central usable field of view while exposing residuals caused by weak or missing path support, shifted responses, unsupported anchors, and missing physical mechanisms. Rather than claiming complete radar-map reconstruction or cross-room generalization, mmRadarTwin establishes a practical systems workflow for constructing, comparing, and diagnosing indoor radar digital twins.

</details>


### [62] [Towards Practical Algorithm Selection for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Medical Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28125)
*Yiheng Xiong,Luisa Gallée,Daniel Santak Wolf,Heiko Hillenhagen,Michael Götz*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A label-free, cross-algorithm criterion to select the best UDA model and hyperparameters for deployment in unlabeled target domains, by building a reference from agreement among multiple candidate models and selecting the one aligned with that reference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: In clinical UDA, target labels are unavailable for evaluation; selecting the right algorithm and hyperparameters is critical for deployment without labeled data.

Method: From a pool of candidate models across algorithms and hyperparameters: within each algorithm, use multiple label-free signals to nominate a model; aggregate the nominated models across algorithms to form a target-specific reference prediction; score each candidate by agreement with the reference and pick the top-scoring candidate for deployment. Evaluated on eight datasets (four brain MRI and four chest X-ray) across seven transfer scenarios.

Result: The proposed selection criterion outperforms alternative label-free selection strategies and remains robust across different algorithm pools and datasets.

Conclusion: This work advances practical deployment of UDA in clinical settings by providing a label-free, aggregation-based model selection criterion that reduces reliance on target labels.

Abstract: Numerous unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) algori-thms exist, but for clinical practice, selecting the best-suited one along with proper hyperparameters often remains unclear, as the unlabeled deployment (target) domain prevents direct evaluation. We propose a label-free criterion that jointly selects the algorithm and hyperparameters for UDA. Given a pool of candidate models from multiple algorithms trained with different hyperparameters, our approach scores each candidate against an agreement reference, and selects the one with the highest score. The agreement reference is constructed in two levels without using target labels. First, we leverage multiple label-free selection signals, using each to nominate a model within every algorithm. Second, the nominated models are aggregated across algorithms to form a reference prediction for each unlabeled target sample. The candidate whose predictions agree most with this reference is then selected for deployment. Experimental results on four brain MRI and four chest X-ray datasets across seven clinically relevant transfer scenarios show that our method achieves better selection performance than other methods and remains effective across different algorithm pools. Our approach takes a step towards practical, label-free algorithm selection for clinical deployment of UDA.

</details>


### [63] [Face and Voice Cross-modal Association with Learning Convex Feature Embedding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28129)
*Taewan Kim,Jiwoo Kang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposed a cross-modal face-voice embedding method using a convex-embedding with an intermediate 'feature exists' to align same-person faces and voices; enhanced by cross-modal attention to reduce misclassifications; shows clear improvements on VoxCeleb across verification, matching, and retrieval.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address inter-modal heterogeneity and the prevalence of false positives/negatives in cross-modal face-voice association; prior work focused on cross-modal discrimination rather than consistent cross-modal embedding.

Method: Introduce an intermediary cross-modal feature (feature-existence) to form a convex hull around same-person embeddings; integrate cross-modal attention with convex embedding; train to minimize inter-class discrepancies.

Result: Evaluated on VoxCeleb for verification, matching, retrieval; reported notable improvements over state-of-the-art.

Conclusion: Cross-modal attention and convex embedding effectively align face and voice representations, reducing errors and improving cross-modal tasks.

Abstract: Face-and-voice association learning is one of the most challenging tasks in deep learning. In this paper, we propose a simple but powerful cross-modal feature embedding method for the association of faces and voices. Previous work has studied cross-modal association tasks to establish the correlation between voice clips and facial images. These works have addressed cross-modal discrimination but underestimate the importance of handling heterogeneity in inter-modal features between audio and video, resulting in a lot of false positives and false negatives. To tackle the problem, the proposed method learns the embeddings of cross-modal features by making another feature exist between cross-modal features, facilitating the voice and face features of the same person to be embedded in a convex hull. Moreover, the incorporation of cross-modal attention mechanisms with convex embedding techniques represents a highly effective strategy for the attenuation of false positives and false negatives, accomplished via the minimization of inter-class discrepancies. We exhaustively evaluated our method for cross-modal verification, matching, and retrieval tasks on the large-scale VoxCeleb dataset. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves notable improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.

</details>


### [64] [Collaborative Feature Aggregation for Face Super-Resolution and Robust Re-Identification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28130)
*Juheon Hwang,Taewan Kim,Jiwoo Kang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Transformer-based collaborative feature aggregation across multiple facial observations (time/views) for joint face SR and robust re-id via a cascade SR network, yielding improved SR quality and recognition under degradation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Face SR and re-id degrade under low-quality, single-view data; exploiting correlations across sequences/views with a unified identity representation can improve robustness and accuracy.

Method: Introduce a transformer-based collaborative feature aggregation to unify identity features from multi-sequence/multi-view data; employ a cascade SR network for progressive restoration with gradual feature unification; use the unified identity representation for robust person re-identification.

Result: Experiments show the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art on both face super-resolution and re-identification benchmarks, with consistent improvements and ablations supporting the benefits of joint identity reconstruction and progressive restoration from multiple inputs.

Conclusion: Joint identity reconstruction and progressive image restoration from multiple facial inputs effectively enhance downstream recognition tasks, enabling more robust SR and re-id under challenging conditions.

Abstract: We propose a novel collaborative approach for face super-resolution (SR) and robust person re-identification from sequential or multi-view facial images. Traditional SR methods often suffer from blurring and distortion in faces recovered from poor-quality images due to low resolution. Image- and video-based facial SR methods using facial landmarks or segmentation also have similar challenges. To overcome these limitations, we leverage multiple correlated facial observations, across time or viewpoints, by introducing a transformer-based collaborative feature aggregation method that unifies identity features from multi-sequence or multi-view data. This allows faces in multiple sequences of an individual to contribute to accurately estimating common facial features. Furthermore, we propose a cascade SR network to progressively restore the high-resolution image of the target's face with gradual facial feature unification. The unified identity representation is further utilized in person re-identification scenarios, enabling accurate matching even under severe image degradation. The exhaustive experimental results and comparisons show that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating consistent improvements in both face super-resolution and re-identification performance. Our work highlights the effectiveness of joint identity reconstruction and progressive image restoration from multiple facial inputs in enhancing downstream visual recognition tasks.

</details>


### [65] [Convolutional Neural Shading for High-Quality 3D Reconstruction from Multi-View Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28132)
*Juheon Hwang,Taewan Kim,Heeseok Oh,Jiwoo Kang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A neural shading-based pipeline (CNS) improves 3D reconstruction from multi-view images by capturing local geometry with a convolutional neural shader and a fine-detail displacement network, addressing limitations of single-point geometry in neural rendering and yielding higher-quality shapes and renders than SOTA.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Neural rendering methods (e.g., NeRF) rely largely on single-point surface information (positions, normals), which limits reconstruction of fine local geometry, especially in dark/textureless regions and at image boundaries. There is a need for richer, view-consistent local geometry cues to enhance detail and geometry discontinuities.

Method: Introduce a convolutional neural shading (CNS) pipeline that uses a neural shader to model local shading variations beyond point geometry. Add a fine-detail displacement network that leverages spatial information from surface geometry and correlates neighboring rendering coordinates to learn high-frequency displacements, reducing boundary irregularities. Train with multi-view consistency to produce accurate, high-fidelity 3D shapes and realistic renderings.

Result: Extensive experiments show significant quality improvements in reconstructed shapes and rendered images over current state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating better local detail and fewer artefacts.

Conclusion: The CNS framework addresses the limitations of single-point geometric cues in neural rendering by incorporating a neural shading model and a displacement-based refinement, enabling more accurate high-fidelity 3D reconstruction from multi-view data.

Abstract: We propose a convolutional neural shading (CNS), a novel pipeline to reconstruct high-quality 3D shapes from multi-view images. Several recent studies have used neural radiance fields and other neural differentiable rendering methods to understand 3D geometry. However, these approaches rely on single-point geometric information, such as positions and normals of the surface, leading to a lack of detailed local geometry. Our approach addresses the inherent limitations of single-point information by leveraging a neural shader to capture variations even in dark and textureless regions with a convolutional neural shader, resulting in far more accurate geometry predictions. Additionally, our method mitigates surface irregularities at image boundaries by introducing a fine-detail displacement network, which utilizes spatial information of surface geometry and learns fine displacement details by correlating neighboring values in the rendering coordinates. Through extensive experiments, our proposed method has demonstrated significant quality improvements in the reconstructed shapes and rendered images over current state-of-the-art methods.

</details>


### [66] [What Makes Deep Learning Work for Traditional Chinese Medicine Tongue Diagnosis? A Comprehensive Ablation Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28148)
*Longxia Gao,Linan Wang,Yuhe Han,Junze Geng,Meng Zhang,Hanqing Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Systematic ablation study across 20+ model variants for multi-label tongue-diagnosis imaging, identifying six design principles that improve performance under class imbalance and small to moderate data regimes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Explore the underexamined design space in deep learning for automated tongue diagnosis in TCM and identify robust, generalizable guidelines for multi-label medical image classification with imbalance.

Method: 5-fold cross-validated ablation over 20+ model versions on TongueDx2 (5,109 images, 976 expert labels) and a merged 11,101-sample dataset. Compared six backbones, four loss functions, five augmentation strategies, and six training strategies. Evaluated using weighted-F1.

Result: Best 976-sample model: weighted-F1 0.6625 (ConvNeXt-Tiny, restrained augmentation, weak-group ensemble). Best 11,101-sample model: weighted-F1 0.7761. Six principles: (1) ConvNeXt-Tiny offers parameter efficiency; (2) BCE outperforms Asymmetric Loss by +2.7%; (3) restrained color augmentation is critical; (4) weak-group ensemble replacement (+2.1%) beats probability averaging; (5) data scaling yields +20.6%; (6) expanding from 13 to 45 labels caused catastrophic collapse (0.78 to 0.22).

Conclusion: These principles generalize to multi-label medical image classification with class imbalance and inform design choices for tongue-diagnosis and related tasks.

Abstract: Deep learning has shown promise for automated tongue diagnosis in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), yet the design space remains underexplored. We conducted a systematic ablation study spanning 20+ model versions under rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on TongueDx2 (5,109 images, 976 expert-annotated) and a merged dataset of 11,101 samples. We compared six backbone architectures, four loss functions, five augmentation strategies, and six training strategies. The best 976-sample model achieved weighted-F1 of 0.6625 using ConvNeXt-Tiny with restrained augmentation and weak-group ensemble, while the best 11,101-sample model reached weighted-F1 of 0.7761. Six key design principles emerged: (1) ConvNeXt-Tiny offers optimal parameter efficiency; (2) BCE substantially outperforms Asymmetric Loss (+2.7%); (3) restrained color augmentation is critical; (4) weak-group ensemble replacement (+2.1%) outperforms probability averaging; (5) data scaling yielded +20.6% improvement; (6) expanding from 13 to 45 label dimensions caused catastrophic collapse (0.78 to 0.22). These principles are generalizable to multi-label medical image classification with class imbalance.

</details>


### [67] [OPLD: On-Policy Latent Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28154)
*Shoutai Zhu,Tianyang Xu,Bin Sun,Mingyuan Xu,Yu Liu,Qinzhen Guo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: OPLD transfers reasoning from privileged multimodal Chain-of-Thought into latent representations, yielding improved multimodal reasoning and state-of-the-art results on benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing multimodal CoT methods rely on externally defined traces and visual operations; latent methods align to compressed visual features rather than active reasoning, failing to internalize abstract reasoning. A latent-space distillation of reasoning is needed.

Method: Proposes On-Policy Latent Distillation (OPLD): distills the reasoning capability from privileged multimodal CoT into latent reasoning representations using on-policy training to align latent states with intermediate reasoning steps.

Result: Empirically, OPLD consistently outperforms existing latent reasoning methods across diverse multimodal benchmarks and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple tasks.

Conclusion: Supervising latent representations at the reasoning-process level is more effective for multimodal latent reasoning than conventional feature-level alignment.

Abstract: Interleaved multimodal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves visual reasoning by incorporating auxiliary visual evidence into intermediate reasoning. However, existing approaches remain constrained by externally defined reasoning traces and visual operations, limiting their ability to develop flexible and abstract visual thinking. Reasoning with latent has recently offered a promising direction by internalizing intermediate computation into continuous representations. Nevertheless, existing visual-latent methods mainly supervise latent states through alignment with compressed auxiliary visual features, treating them as proxies for visual observations rather than active reasoning states. Consequently, they capture the provided evidence but fail to fully internalize the abstract reasoning process induced by multimodal CoT. In this paper, we propose OPLD (On-Policy Latent Distillation), a simple framework that transfers the reasoning capability induced by privileged multimodal CoT into latent reasoning representations. Extensive experiments on diverse multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that OPLD consistently outperforms existing latent reasoning methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks. The results suggest that supervising latent representations at the reasoning-process level provides a more effective paradigm for multimodal latent reasoning than conventional feature-level alignment.

</details>


### [68] [S-Avatar: Diffusion-Guided Gaussian Head Avatars from a Single Image](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28164)
*Hail Song,Seokhwan Yang,Jiwon Yang,Woojin Cho,Woontack Woo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Diffusion-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline enabling single-image photorealistic 3D head avatars with FLAME-driven control and a binding template for real-time rendering, achieving superior novel-view and expression consistency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Single-image head avatar reconstruction often lacks 3D consistency under unseen viewpoints, hindering lifelike VR experiences.

Method: Three-stage pipeline: (1) synthesize a high-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) from a single image using a diffusion-based module; (2) align the FLAME head model with 3DGS by optimizing FLAME parameters and spatial transforms; (3) build a binding template to encode spatial relationships between splats and FLAME, enabling real-time rendering by deforming 3DGS with the template.

Result: On public datasets, S-Avatar surpasses state-of-the-art methods in novel-view and expression generation, delivering higher realism and 3D consistency.

Conclusion: Combining diffusion-guided canonical 3DGS generation with FLAME-based control yields efficient, accurate single-image head avatar reconstruction suitable for VR/AR; publicly available project page.

Abstract: We propose S-Avatar, a novel method for generating photorealistic 3D head avatars from a single image using a diffusion-guided 3D model generation module and strategies for animating 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). While single-image head avatar reconstruction is crucial for lifelike Virtual Reality (VR) applications, existing approaches often struggle to preserve 3D consistency under unseen viewpoints. S-Avatar addresses this limitation through a three-stage pipeline. First, a high-resolution 3DGS is synthesized directly from a single image using a diffusion-based Gaussian splat generation module. Next, the parametric head model FLAME is aligned with the generated 3DGS by optimizing its parameters and spatial transformations. Finally, to adapt the 3DGS to FLAME variations, we construct a binding template that encodes the spatial relationship between the initial splats and FLAME. The dynamic 3D head avatar can then be rendered in real time by deforming the 3DGS with the binding template. By combining diffusion-guided canonical 3DGS generation with FLAME-based control, our method achieves efficient and accurate reconstruction with enhanced 3D consistency. Evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that S-Avatar outperforms state-of-the-art methods in novel-view and expression generation, achieving superior realism and consistency. Consequently, our approach represents a significant advance in accessible avatar creation, applicable to a wide range of VR/AR applications. The project page is available at https://github.com/hailsong/savatar.

</details>


### [69] [Think with Extra-Image: A Farmland Segmentation Agent Driven by Spatio-Temporal Information Gain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28186)
*Haiyang Wu,Weiliang Mu,Zhuofei Du,Dandan Zhong,Kaijie Shi,Haifeng Li,Chao Tao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Dynamic FRSI segmentation via an information-bottleneck agent (FarmSeeker) that queries extra spatio-temporal data to resolve ambiguity, with a global high-res benchmark (GSFS-Bench) and demonstrated improved segmentation stability.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: FRSI segmentation is often ambiguous when relying on a single current image due to phenology and spatial context; relevant spatio-temporal information lies beyond the current frame, necessitating an information-guided, interactive approach.

Method: Define FRSI segmentation as a dynamic decision process guided by information gain; introduce FarmSeeker agent that identifies ambiguous regions, reasons about their causes, and queries extra spatio-temporal information on demand; construct GSFS-Bench for reasoning-querying evaluation.

Result: FarmSeeker achieves more stable segmentation performance than existing methods on the GSFS-Bench benchmark, demonstrating the value of on-demand spatio-temporal information and dynamic decision-making in FRSI segmentation.

Conclusion: Framing FRSI segmentation as an information-bottleneck, dynamic querying task yields robust performance and outlines a new benchmark; FarmSeeker provides a viable path toward integrating extra information for improved remote-sensing segmentation.

Abstract: Existing farmland remote sensing image (FRSI) segmentation follows a "Think with Intra-Image" paradigm, assuming that the current image contains sufficient visual evidence for reliable segmentation. Yet farmland appearance varies with phenology and spatial context and is often confused with other land-cover, making instantaneous, local observations inadequate. Thus, segmentation ambiguity stems not only from limited model representation, but more fundamentally from the required spatio-temporal information lying beyond the current image. Based on this insight, we redefine FRSI segmentation from an information bottleneck perspective as a dynamic decision process driven by task-relevant extra spatio-temporal information gain. We further propose FarmSeeker, a dynamic FRSI segmentation agent that identifies ambiguous regions, reasons about their causes, and queries extra spatio-temporal information on demand for accurate segmentation. To evaluate FarmSeeker, we construct GSFS-Bench, the first global-scale, high-resolution FRSI segmentation benchmark that supports reasoning-querying. Experiments show that FarmSeeker achieves more stable segmentation performance than existing methods. The project is publicly available at: https://withoutocean.github.io/FarmSeeker/

</details>


### [70] [Scaling Vision-Language Models Is Not Enough to Mitigate Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28211)
*Ioannis Sarridis,Ioannis Kompatsiaris,Symeon Papadopoulos*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Large-scale study shows scale alone does not guarantee robustness to spurious correlations in vision-language models; data quality/curation and benchmark choice play larger roles, with architectural effects being highly context-dependent.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand how model size, training data, and architecture interact with bias and robustness in vision-language models across a wide set of models and benchmarks.

Method: Empirical evaluation of 194 publicly available VLMs (16 families) across 24 training datasets, assessed on three benchmarks: ImageNet (overall), CelebA (single-attribute bias), UrbanCars (multi-attribute bias). Used Spearman correlations between model scale and performance, examined worst-group accuracy, compared curated vs uncurated data, and analyzed architectural choices (e.g., patch size, resolution).

Result: Scale-performance correlation weakens with bias severity (ρ=0.68 on ImageNet to ρ=0.48 on single-attribute bias to ρ=0.05 on multi-attribute bias). Training data size/quality more consistently relate to worst-group accuracy. Curated datasets yield up to 25% gains over uncurated at similar scale. Architectural effects are highly context-dependent, varying by bias type and spatial distribution within images.

Conclusion: Scale alone is insufficient to ensure robustness to spurious correlations in VLMs; dataset curation and benchmark selection are critical, and architectural choices should consider the specific bias characteristics and their spatial resolution.

Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP are now foundational to multimodal systems, yet their robustness to spurious correlations remains poorly understood at scale. We present the first large-scale empirical study of 194 publicly available VLMs, including 16 model families, covering a wide range of model sizes, 24 training datasets, and three evaluation benchmarks, namely ImageNet (overall performance), CelebA (typical single-attribute bias), and UrbanCars (complex multi-attribute biases). Across these settings, the Spearman correlation between model scale and performance weakens as evaluation shifts from ImageNet ($ρ{=}0.68$) to single-attribute ($ρ{=}0.48$) and further to multi-attribute ($ρ{=}0.05$) bias benchmarks. In contrast, properties of the training data (size and quality) show more consistent relationships with worst-group accuracy across both bias benchmarks. Notably, curated datasets yield improvements of up to 25% over uncurated alternatives at a comparable scale. Finally, the effect of architectural choices (e.g., patch size, image resolution) is highly context-dependent, varying with the nature of the benchmark, including the type of bias and its spatial distribution within images.

</details>


### [71] [FaithEyes: Towards Faithful Tool Use via Multi-Agent Process-Image Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28225)
*Haoqing Wang,Xingrun Xing,Wei Xia,Ziheng Li,Yehui Tang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FaithEyes introduces a self-judging, multi-agent framework to improve tool faithfulness in agentic vision-language models (VLMs) by having a judge evaluate the usefulness of each processed image, injecting this judgment into tool observations to guide reasoning and scaling the tool reward. It also employs a self-subagent at inference to replace external judges, and uses a two-stage SFT+RL training on adapted data. It achieves competitive/superior performance and markedly better tool faithfulness across visual perception and reasoning benchmarks, with code available at the project homepage.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Prevailing tool-use in agentic VLMs often involves unfaithful or irrelevant tool calls; rewards fail to distinguish useful vs useless tool calls, and tool feedback lacks usefulness signals. This leads to wasted computation and reliance on priors rather than retrieved evidence. A train-test-consistent, faithful tool-use framework is needed.

Method: FaithEyes builds a multi-agent system where a VLM acts as a tool-use judge to determine whether each processed image helps answer the question. The judgment is injected into the tool observation to guide subsequent reasoning and is used to scale the tool reward by the helpful-tool ratio to reduce reward hacking. At evaluation, the model itself serves as the subagent to judge tool calls, removing reliance on external models. Training uses a two-stage SFT + RL pipeline on adapted open-source data.

Result: FaithEyes achieves competitive or superior accuracy on visual perception and reasoning benchmarks while markedly improving tool faithfulness, reducing misaligned/counterproductive tool calls.

Conclusion: The framework provides a principled approach to faithful tool use in agentic VLMs through internal self-judgment and reward shaping, maintaining train-test consistency and showing strong empirical gains. Open-source code is available.

Abstract: Agentic vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave textual reasoning with explicit tool calls such as cropping and code-based image manipulation, have emerged as a compelling paradigm for reliable and interpretable multimodal reasoning. However, recent studies have revealed that such models often use tools unfaithfully. Many process images are irrelevant to the question (e.g., the tool crops the wrong region or misses the queried target), yet the call still receives full credit and the model still answers correctly. Such decorative or misaligned tool calls waste computation and reveal that the model leans on prior knowledge or the original image rather than the evidence it retrieves. This may stem from two limitations of prevailing methods: the tool reward fails to distinguish useful from useless calls, and tool feedback carries no signal of usefulness. To this end, we introduce FaithEyes, a multi-agent self-judging framework. Concretely, we use a VLM to judge whether each process image helps answer the question. The judgement is injected into the reasoning context as part of the tool observation to help subsequent reasoning, and meanwhile is used to scale the tool reward by the helpful-tool ratio to suppress reward hacking. To keep judgement available at evaluation and thus ensure train-test consistency, we further design a multi-agent framework where the model itself serves as a subagent to judge the tool calls from main agent, eliminating any dependence on an external model at inference. Training via a two-stage SFT + RL pipeline on adapted open-source data, FaithEyes attains competitive or superior accuracy across visual perception and reasoning benchmarks, while markedly improving tool faithfulness. The homepage is at https://github.com/Mosi-AI/FaithEyes.

</details>


### [72] [EgoGenesis: Egocentric World-Action Modeling with Online Anchored Projective Memory and Action-3D RoPE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28243)
*Zexuan Yan,Yuzhou Wu,Yue Ma,Zonghang He,Kaibo Yin,Xiaobing Tu,Yinggui Wang,Jinkui Ren,Xiantao Zhang,Shijian Wang,Jinghong Liu,Linfeng Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A geometry-aware egocentric video synthesizer augments scarce real data with controllable, high-quality synthetic trajectories, improving long-horizon manipulation fidelity and downstream robot-task generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the scarcity and cost of diverse egocentric manipulation data; enable scalable generation of controllable, high-fidelity videos to improve sim-to-real transfer and generalization for embodied AI.

Method: Two geometry-aware conditioning mechanisms on a pretrained video generation prior: (1) Online Anchored Projective Memory (OAPM) maintains a fixed first-frame 3D scene anchor and periodically refreshes recent state during autoregression; (2) Action-3D Rotary Position Embedding (A3D-RoPE) encodes end-effector motion in camera-aware 3D rotary coordinates and injects this action geometry into skeleton-to-video cross-attention.

Result: The approach yields higher visual fidelity, geometric stability, and action alignment in long egocentric rollouts. Quantitatively, augmenting 400 real trajectories with 400 synthetic ones improves real-robot success from 77% to 84% (single-arm) and from 53% to 70% (dual-arm) on WAM tasks.

Conclusion: Geometry-aware conditioning substantially enhances the utility of synthetic egocentric videos for expanding scarce data, leading to marked improvements in downstream robot manipulation generalization.

Abstract: Egocentric video offers rich manipulation experience for embodied AI, yet collecting diverse egocentric data across scenes, objects, motions, and embodiments remains costly. We present \method, an egocentric world-action simulator that synthesizes controllable, high-quality manipulation videos to expand scarce real-world training data. \method{} builds on a pretrained video generation prior and introduces two geometry-aware conditioning mechanisms. Online Anchored Projective Memory (OAPM) preserves a first-frame 3D scene anchor while periodically refreshing a recent state during autoregressive generation. Action-3D Rotary Position Embedding (A3D-RoPE) encodes end-effector motion with camera-aware 3D rotary coordinates, injecting action geometry into skeleton-to-video cross-attention for precise control. Together, these components improve visual fidelity, geometric stability, and action alignment in long egocentric rollouts. Moreover, augmenting 400 real trajectories with 400 \method-generated trajectories improves out-of-distribution real-robot success from 77\% to 84\% on single-arm tasks and from 53\% to 70\% on dual-arm tasks, demonstrating that the synthesized data substantially improve downstream WAM generalization.

</details>


### [73] [Space2Ground 2.0: A Multi-Source Dataset and Framework for Agricultural Monitoring through Fusion of Street-Level and Satellite Imagery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28247)
*Iason Tsardanidis,Alkiviadis Koukos,George Choumos,Vasileios Sitokontantinou,Charalampos Kontoes*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Space2Ground 2.0 fuses Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral time series, and crowd-sourced street-level imagery to create parcel-linked, analysis-ready data for agricultural monitoring; it yields a sizable open benchmark over Cyprus (2022) with 46k annotated street-level images linked to 8.6k parcels and demonstrates improved crop classification when combining modalities.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Limitations of satellite-only, cloud-affected optical monitoring; need fine-grained, scalable parcel-level information and verification in agriculture; leverage crowdsourced street-level data to complement satellite observations.

Method: A largely automated pipeline performs semantic filtering, image quality assessment, viewpoint-based parcel association, and dataset refinement to transform large volumes of crowdsourced imagery into parcel-linked data. It integrates Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral time series with Mapillary street-level imagery and links outputs to agricultural parcels in Cyprus for the 2022 growing season.

Result: Creation of 46,050 annotated street-level images selected from 900k+, linked to 8,581 parcels. Parcel-level crop classification experiments show street-level imagery provides complementary, fine-scale visual information that enhances classification when integrated with satellite time series.

Conclusion: Space2Ground 2.0 offers an open benchmark dataset and reproducible methodology for multimodal agricultural monitoring, enabling visual verification, reducing field inspections, and informing data-driven policy.

Abstract: Accurate and scalable parcel-level agricultural monitoring remains challenging because satellite Earth Observation alone provides only an overhead perspective of agricultural parcels, while optical observations are further affected by cloud-induced temporal gaps. This paper presents Space2Ground 2.0, a multi-source framework integrating Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral time series with geo-tagged street-level imagery acquired using vehicle-mounted cameras and shared through the Mapillary platform. A largely automated processing pipeline performs semantic filtering, image quality assessment, viewpoint-based parcel association, and dataset refinement, transforming large volumes of crowdsourced imagery into parcel-linked, analysis-ready data. Applied over Cyprus during the 2022 growing season, the pipeline produced a curated dataset of 46,050 annotated street-level images, selected from an initial collection exceeding 900,000 images and linked with satellite information for 8,581 agricultural parcels. The practical value of the dataset was assessed through parcel-level crop classification experiments using both single- and multi-source observations. The results demonstrate that street-level imagery provides complementary fine-scale visual information that enhances classification when integrated with satellite time series. Overall, Space2Ground 2.0 provides an openly available benchmark dataset and a reproducible methodology for multimodal agricultural monitoring, with potential applications in visual verification, reduced reliance on costly field inspections, and data-driven agricultural policy implementation.

</details>


### [74] [TARS: Timestep-Aware Data Scaling for 3D-Free Video Re-Shooting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28261)
*Jiwen Liu,Shujuan Li,Xiaohan Li,Zijie Meng,Xinyue Liu,Yulong Xu,Yan Zhou,Guoxin Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: 3D-free video re-shooting with text-driven viewpoint control via TARS; self-supervised training without paired data or 3D reconstruction; robust camera/viewpoint manipulation including reverse-angle and perspective switching, aided by data scaling and joint textual-camera conditioning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Limitations of explicit 3D priors (reconstruction quality, unseen regions) and reliance on scarce paired-reconstruction data hinder generalization; text-driven control offers flexible viewpoint manipulation.

Method: Proposes TARS, a 3D-free video re-shooting framework. Uses timestep-wise sensitivity analysis to show camera motion forms in high-noise stages. Employs self-supervised training to learn camera dynamics and visual representations without paired re-shoot data or 3D reconstruction. Enhances robustness via data scaling and joint textual-camera conditioning, enabling large-motion synthesis beyond source view, reverse-angle re-shooting, and perspective switching.

Result: Extensive experiments indicate TARS achieves more accurate and temporally consistent camera control than prior methods, with plausible beyond-source-view synthesis and support for reverse-angle and perspective changes.

Conclusion: TARS demonstrates that 3D-free, text-driven camera control is feasible and effective for video re-shooting, enabling robust viewpoint manipulation without heavy supervision or 3D priors.

Abstract: Video re-shooting aims to regenerate videos with controllable camera motion and viewpoint. Existing methods rely on explicit 3D priors, which are limited by reconstruction quality and often perform poorly when synthesizing previously unseen regions, or on paired videos with different camera trajectories, whose scarcity hinders generalization. We revisit video re-shooting through text-driven semantic viewpoint specification, enabling control over shot scale, viewing angle, and first-/third-person perspective. To this end, we propose TARS, a 3D-free video re-shooting paradigm. Timestep-wise sensitivity analysis reveals that camera motion is primarily established during high-noise stages, where coarse spatiotemporal structures are formed. Based on this insight, we introduce self-supervised training to learn camera dynamics and fundamental visual representations without paired re-shooting data or 3D reconstruction. Through data scaling and joint textual-camera conditioning, TARS supports robust camera and viewpoint control, plausibly synthesizing regions beyond the source view under large camera motions while enabling reverse-angle re-shooting and perspective switching. Extensive experiments show that TARS provides more accurate and temporally consistent camera control than prior methods. Project Page: https://ymlinfeng.github.io/TARS.github.io/

</details>


### [75] [Theia: Large-Scale Multimodal Captioning and Automated Validation of the Incidents1M Dataset for Data-Free Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28269)
*Simone Giano,Lorenzo Severini,Alessandro Galdelli,Adriano Mancini*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A scalable, LLM-validated multimodal disaster dataset is built by recovering 100k images from Incidents1M and generating captions with two Qwen3.5 models, validated by an image-blind LLM judge to emulate student modality gaps for Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: High-quality multimodal data is essential for VLMs in critical disaster domains and for effective DFKD. Existing datasets either lack descriptive text or suffer from misalignment, hindering knowledge transfer.

Method: Recover 100,000 images from Incidents1M and generate captions using two Qwen3.5 architectures (4B dense and 35B MoE). Validate captions with an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline using Qwen3.5-9B to simulate the modality gap of student models during data-free distillation.

Result: Semantic agreement between the two captioners is high (78.65/100). Automated evaluation shows conservative captioning (precision 77.6%, recall 46.0%), reducing false positives and highlighting human annotation inconsistencies in ground truth.

Conclusion: Offers a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation in disaster-response contexts.

Abstract: The deployment of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in critical domains like disaster management requires high-quality multimodal datasets, especially for transferring knowledge via Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD). However, existing datasets in this domain either entirely lack descriptive text, such as Incidents1M, or suffer from severe text-image semantic misalignment, such as CrisisMMD. In this work, we present a novel methodology to construct and automatically validate a large-scale multimodal dataset for disaster response. Starting from the vision-only Incidents1M, we successfully recovered 100,000 images and generated high-fidelity textual descriptions using two distinct Qwen3.5 architectures: a 4B dense model and a 35B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model. To ensure the generated captions provide reliable semantic anchoring for DFKD, we introduce an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge validation pipeline leveraging Qwen3.5-9B. By intentionally obscuring the original image from the judge, this evaluator accurately simulates the modality gap of the student model during data-free distillation. Our evaluation across 173,179 label pairs demonstrates a high semantic agreement (78.65/100) between the two architectures. Furthermore, the automated evaluation reveals a conservative captioning behaviour, characterized by a high Precision (77.6%) and low Recall (46.0%). This minimizes the false positive noise, while simultaneously exposing underlying human annotation inconsistencies in the original ground truth. This work provides a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation.

</details>


### [76] [MSCM-net: A hyperspectral image classiffcation method based on multi-scale convolution and Mamba](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28277)
*Jianjun Chen,Linlin Wang,Lifang Chang,Limin Huo,Shujiang Song,Yanjia Zhao,Mingwei Shao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A multi-scale CNN and Mamba-based MSCM-net for hyperspectral image classification, with MCSE and dual-branch fusion, achieving strong accuracy while reducing computation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Hyperspectral image classification is challenged by CNN/Transformer locality constraints and high computational cost. A model combining local multi-scale feature extraction with long-range modeling aims to improve accuracy and efficiency.

Method: Proposes MSCM-net architecture: multi-scale CNN+Mamba blocks; MCSE module combining multi-scale convolutions with SENet for channel-wise weighting; dual-branch feature aggregation to fuse central pixel spectral information with surrounding spatial context; stacked Mamba blocks for long sequence modeling.

Result: Experiments on three benchmark datasets show advanced classification performance and reduced computational complexity.

Conclusion: MSC M-net effectively integrates local multi-scale features with long-range modeling, achieving competitive accuracy with lower compute in hyperspectral image classification.

Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging is widely used in remote sensing and engineering. Therefore, research on its classification methods is crucial. While CNN and Transformer-based methods have advanced, they still face locality constraints and high computational complexity. To address these issues, we propose an innovative hyperspectral image classification model, MSCM-net. Specifically, first of all, a model architecture combining multi-scale CNN and Mamba is proposed. It consists of a multi-scale feature extraction module (MCSE) and multiple stacked Mamba blocks, which integrates the local feature extraction capability of multi-scale CNN and the long sequence modeling advantage of Mamba. Secondly, the proposed MCSE module consists of multi-scale convolution and SENet. Convolution kernels of different scales extract local information with different receptive fields, enhancing the fusion of spatial and spectral information. Meanwhile, the SENet enables the model to automatically learn the importance of each channel in the multi-scale features. Furthermore, we also propose a dual-branch feature aggregation module, which further effectively extracts and integrates the spectral information contained in the central pixel and the spatial information in the surrounding pixels. Our model has undergone numerous experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets. The experimental results show that MSCM-net can achieve advanced classification performance while reducing computational complexity.

</details>


### [77] [Beyond Visual Ambiguity: Guiding Robust Monocular Depth Estimation in Challenging Scenarios via Detailed Long Captions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28285)
*Junrui Zhang,Jiaqi Li,Yiran Wang,Liao Shen,Zhiguo Cao*

Main category: cs.CV
